sourceBinding: Changes relative to sourceRevision are identified by the exact source hashes below; the enclosing commit carries the implementation. Full canonical administration/dispatch integration remains in progress.
claims: Canonical pending creation, exact-term approval and grant issuance are durable and separate from capability execution. Request decision, grant, lifecycle event and retry result commit together.

Independent SQLite workers race two approvals and one denial. Exactly one terminal request decision wins, with exactly one grant only if approval wins. Injected event-write failure rolls back all approval changes.
Approval binds the existing request revision, confirmation digest, class and explicit deadlines. Invalid/current-owner/provider scope, stale terms and backwards or expired time prevent issuance.

Recorded approve/deny/revoke commands replay their original results without new mutation; changed content conflicts. Reopening the database and replaying approval after revocation cannot revive the grant.

Canonical eligibility is non-consuming and validates the selected grant, authenticated context, exact Assistant/endpoint/environment/operation/version, target/data subsets, class bindings and time/lifecycle restrictions. Empty data scope grants no data access. Callback inputs are isolated and changed authority context is rejected.

Request history and grant events preserve original bytes and hashes. Corrupt or transplanted record contents and inconsistent grant event histories are withheld. Legacy coarse grant rows are unchanged.
